Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old man with known asthma presents via telehealth with 3 hours of acute chest tightness, mild exertional dyspnea, wheeze, and non-productive cough following a recent cold; has been off both ICS and SABA for ~1 week. Impression: acute asthma exacerbation, likely viral-triggered and worsened by lapse in controller/reliever use.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute chest tightness.
- Onset/duration: Began ~3 hours prior to consult.
- Course/progression: Persistent since onset; mild exertional dyspnea; not short of breath at rest.
- Character: Tightness (not pain); reports feeling unable to take a full breath at times.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Wheeze.
  - Non-productive cough; slightly worse at night.
  - Recent URTI last week (sore throat, runny nose, “under the weather”); nasal symptoms improving; cough persisting.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors:
  - Worse with exertion (stairs).
  - No inhaler use in past week due to running out.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain; no productive sputum; not SOB at rest; no fever reported.
- Patient goals/concerns: Wants to ensure safety; worried about severity given prior intubation; needs inhaler refills.

Past Medical History:
- Asthma:
  - Background: Since childhood; severe exacerbation requiring intubation and hospitalization at ~16–17 years.
  - Current control: Worsened after recent URI and 1 week without inhalers.
  - Complications: Prior intubation (teenage years).
- Atopy/allergy-related conditions:
  - Allergic rhinitis/hay fever.
  - Dust allergy.
  - Childhood eczema.
  - Childhood milk protein allergy.
- Medications:
  - Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler PRN; ran out ~1 week ago (dose/route/frequency not documented).
  - Beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) inhaler maintenance; ran out ~1 week ago (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies:
  - Drug allergies: No known drug allergies.
  - Environmental: Dust; hay fever.

Social History:
- Education/occupation: University student; was away at university last week.
- Tobacco: Not documented.
- Alcohol: Not documented.
- Recreational drugs: Not documented.
- Other: No peak flow meter available.

Family History:
- Mother: Eczema.
- Father: Asthma.

Physical Examination:
- Telehealth visit; no vitals or physical exam performed.
- Patient able to speak in full sentences; not short of breath at rest.

Investigations:
- None performed. No peak flow or oxygen saturation available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute asthma exacerbation (likely viral-triggered; worsened by lapse in ICS/SABA)
  - Assessment: Wheeze, chest tightness, non-productive cough, recent URI, increased exertional dyspnea, and 1 week without controller/reliever support high likelihood.
  - Plan:
    - Prescribe SABA (salbutamol/Ventolin) inhaler for PRN relief (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Prescribe ICS (beclomethasone/Clenil Modulite) for maintenance therapy (dose/route/frequency not documented); resume daily use once improved.
    - Oral steroids: Prescribed steroid tablets for 5 days, 2 tablets each morning (specific medication/dose not documented).
    - Spacer: Provide spacer and instructions for proper use.
    - Education/safety net:
      - If salbutamol is needed more frequently than every 3 hours, seek medical attention.
      - Seek urgent care for worsening shortness of breath, increasing chest tightness/pain, light-headedness, or any concerning deterioration.
      - Reviewed possible steroid side effects: mood changes, elevated blood sugar, rash, nausea, headaches.
    - Rest and activity: Advise rest until improvement; time off work discussed; self-certification up to 7 days mentioned.
- Issue 2: Post-viral cough/bronchial hyperreactivity
  - Assessment: Recent URI with lingering cough may contribute and overlap with asthma symptoms.
  - Plan:
    - Continue ICS maintenance and SABA PRN as above.
    - Monitor symptom resolution; return/seek care if persistent or worsening.
- Issue 3: Medication lapse/non-availability
  - Assessment: Ran out of both ICS and SABA ~1 week ago, likely contributing to loss of control.
  - Plan:
    - Send prescriptions within the hour per clinician plan.
    - Encourage medication adherence; ensure ongoing supply of inhalers.
    - Consider keeping spacer and backup inhalers accessible, especially when traveling (education provided).

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Acute asthma exacerbation (High): Known asthma with atopic background; recent URI; current wheeze/chest tightness; 1 week without ICS/SABA; exertional dyspnea.
- Post-viral bronchial hyperreactivity/acute viral bronchitis (Moderate): Persistent non-productive cough after URI; can overlap with asthma symptoms.
- Community-acquired pneumonia (Low): Cough and dyspnea present, but no fever, sputum, pleuritic pain, or focal findings; not SOB at rest.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (HR, RR, BP, SpO2), peak flow or spirometry, detailed inhaler dosing/frequency, clear action plan thresholds beyond SABA > every 3 hours, smoking/alcohol/substance history, vaccination status (e.g., flu), objective exam.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; brief audio dropout acknowledged during steroid discussion.
